_readme: The 9-slide webinar storyline Alex describes at 46:59-48:09 in the 2026-09-04 sales training. He was pointing at a list on his screen ('it's like 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9') and narrated each step aloud. These are the STEPS - the job each slide does - not the headlines. Headlines are written per prospect from the brief.
_lineage: Fireflies transcript -> the brief (extracted_data) -> these slides. Every slide declares the brief field it reads from in 'source'. Where source is null the brief has no field for it yet and the copy here is INFERRED - Geri's transcript-to-brief step needs to start emitting those four.
_style: Sparse and instantly legible. Alex: 'just one sentence, like really'. Nine slides in 'two, three minutes' is roughly fifteen seconds each. Each slide is a headline, a sub-line that completes the thought, and at most one supporting line. A COO reading it at a glance must know what the slide is claiming before they finish it.
_case_study_warning: Slide 6 is the PROSPECT'S case study - one of THEIR clients, shown to THEIR audience. It is NOT a Quantum Scaling client. The QS case-study library (Airtable) is used on the Lead List and Calendar Invite, where we are proving OUR results to the prospect. Different direction. Do not wire Airtable into this slide.

slides.purpose: State the one thing they haven't considered.
slides.headline: Your margin isn't leaking in the machines.
slides.sub: It's leaking in the handoffs between them.
slides.line: 90 minutes for operations leaders carrying cost they can't see on any report.

slides.purpose: Let them self-identify in one read.
slides.headline: You run operations at a plant of 50 to 500 people.
slides.sub: Cost per unit is creeping up and nobody can tell you exactly why.
slides.line: Industrial and manufacturing firms across North America and Western Europe.

slides.purpose: Name the thing they live with daily.
slides.headline: Every handoff costs you time nobody measures.
slides.sub: Shift to shift. Cell to cell. Production to quality.
slides.line: Your machines run at spec. The gaps between them are where the hours go — and no line on your P&L is called “handoff”.
slides.inferred_from: Derived from extracted_data.webinar_angle ('why industrial firms lose margin in the handoffs, not the machines'), stated from the COO's seat. NOT from extracted_data.customer_pain — that field holds the PROSPECT'S lead-generation problem, which a COO is not watching this webinar to hear about.

slides.purpose: Make a year of inaction concrete, in their money.
slides.headline: A quarter of your changeover time is waste.
slides.sub: On a $40M cost base, that is real EBITDA walking out every year.
slides.line: We use the low end of what we've measured elsewhere, not the best case. The number on your floor is almost certainly bigger.
slides.inferred_from: Alex 47:15 — 'make the problem big and demonstrate the impact of not changing, just one sentence'. Sized from the ICP's own cost base, and stated conservatively per Alex 48:41 ('always calculate with the lowest possible inputs… I really want to go as low as somehow possible'). The brief has no ICP-side cost-of-inaction field.

slides.purpose: Show the destination in their units.
slides.headline: Cost per unit down 18 to 30%.
slides.line: Same machines. Same people. No capital spend.

slides.purpose: One plant that already did it.
slides.headline: A 200-person plastics manufacturer in Ohio.
slides.sub: Changeover time cut 40%. $1.1M back a year.
slides.before: Changeover ate a full shift. The cost sat invisible inside overhead.
slides.after: 40% faster changeover. $1.1M annualised, straight to the bottom line.
slides.note: The PROSPECT'S client, not a Quantum Scaling client. Never wire the QS Airtable library into this slide.

slides.purpose: Remove the fear of a long, vague engagement.
slides.headline: You'll know inside 90 days whether it's working.
slides.sub: Weeks 1–2 we measure. Weeks 3–8 we change one line. Then you decide.
slides.line: No plant-wide rollout on day one. We prove it on a single cell first, on your numbers.
slides.inferred_from: Written from the ICP's seat — a COO's journey through the engagement. The earlier draft used Alex's reverse-engineer of invite volume (51:39), which is how QS sells to the PROSPECT, not how the prospect delivers to a COO. Wrong audience. The brief has no ICP-side timeline field.

slides.purpose: Say their objections out loud before they do.
slides.headline: You've been burned by consultants before.

risks.answer: We change one line and leave it running. You keep the method, not a slide deck.
One cell, off your critical path, until the numbers hold.
We measure. Your supervisors keep running the floor.
Measured against your baseline, in your finance team's numbers, not ours.

slides.inferred_from: Alex names four risk categories at 47:54 (investment, failure, communication gap, time). Those are the CATEGORIES; the wording here is what each one sounds like in a COO's head, because that is who is watching. Answers are structural rather than guarantee-based, per Alex 35:11: 'you only use guarantees if you really need it.'

slides.purpose: One ask. Nothing to weigh up.
slides.headline: You could do this yourself.
slides.sub: Most operations teams can't spare the six months it takes to find where the hours go.
slides.line: We've already done it. Your supervisors keep running the floor — we bring the method and the measurement.
slides.inferred_from: Lloyd's direction 2026-09-07: make the final slide a single clean call to action — 'doing this yourself is going to be very difficult, we can do it for you.' NOTE this is a deliberate divergence from Alex 47:59, who asked for 'three key CTAs'. Lloyd's call: one ask on the closing slide beats three, because three is a decision and one is a next step. If Alex wants the three back, the earlier version is in git history at d7c04fc.
slides.cta_note: 30 minutes. You keep the analysis either way.

_inferred_note: Slides 4, 7, 8 and 9 have no brief field yet. Their copy is inferred from the 2026-09-04 sales-training transcript, where Alex teaches his method for each. Every one records its derivation and timestamp in 'inferred_from' so it can be checked against the tape. Slide 9's third CTA is left BLANK on purpose: Alex named only two.
_audience: WHOSE SEAT THIS IS WRITTEN FROM — read before editing a single line. Three audiences stack in DealForge and it is easy to write for the wrong one. (1) Quantum Scaling builds the tool. (2) The PROSPECT is the firm buying QS's system — here, Arcline Operations Group, a consulting firm. (3) The prospect's ICP is who actually WATCHES these slides — here, a COO or VP Operations at a 50-500 person industrial manufacturer. EVERY WORD ON THESE SLIDES IS ADDRESSED TO (3). A line about Arcline's retainers, deal size, close rate or lead flow is meaningless to a COO and instantly signals the deck was not built for them. CAUTION: the brief mixes the two. webinar_angle, result_delivered, case_study and positioning describe the ICP's world and are safe to use. customer_pain, goals, deal_size, close_rate and sales_cycle describe the PROSPECT'S OWN business and must never appear on a slide.
